issues.description: The problem text instructs that the SealSaloon.stock should be a shared (static) attribute but also says these attributes should be initialized in the SealSaloon constructor. Static fields cannot be properly initialized per-instance in an instance constructor, so this is a contradictory requirement and will confuse students about whether stock should be static and where to initialize it.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the intended design: either (A) make stock a static final field and state it should be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer, or (B) keep stock as an instance final field and require initialization in the constructor. Update the problem statement to remove the conflicting instruction about constructor initialization when stock is static.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement shows acceptSupplyDelivery as a public method (+), but the solution implements acceptSupplyDelivery with package-private visibility (no access modifier). This visibility mismatch between the specification and the provided implementation may confuse students about the expected method accessibility.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility consistent: either change the solution to declare public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(...) or update the UML/problem statement to indicate package-private visibility if that was the intended scope. Prefer making it public as the diagram shows public methods.
